notes: Check batch 2026-10-23-check: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All rc 0, uncommitted true, head 83e7f5b and one skill_hash; each model_id matches its tier. The only other model name in the transcripts is claude-opus-5-5 at .shape.tools.model in the api-request-shape record, a model option in a tool definition, not an answering model. Each transcript contains the reworded head-rule sentence ("A head binds what selects its clause") and the new required-keys paragraph ("is dot access written long"), so the runs read the working-tree text. All four read SKILL.md only, with Read, and no reference file; Expected reads is none, so all four meet it. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules: git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ (working tree) touches two rules in this case's list and one sentence outside it (the crash-report sentence in ex_unit.md; no run writes tests). "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" gains three paragraphs (a body pattern that pulls one atom key or struct field is dot access written long; a dot chain for nested required fields; Map.fetch/2 where absent and nil differ). No run has a body pattern on one key, a dot chain into the payload or a Map.get; required keys are read by head patterns and Map.fetch helpers. haiku-1's data["customer_email"] and data["failure_reason"] (lines 108-109) read keys its Payment struct leaves out of @enforce_keys, so they are optional and allowed by the heading; the new nil-versus-absent sentence does not apply because haiku-1 wants nil for both. The verdict in all four runs is clean and is decided by the unchanged first paragraph. "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" is rewritten; the sentences that decide this batch are "A head binds what selects its clause: a value matched against a literal, a value a guard reads, or a key whose presence selects, because another clause catches the input that lacks it.", "A head `mix format` wraps only to move a long guard onto its own line is fine as wrapped" and "those keys select the clause by their presence, so they belong in the head even when the guard reads none of them."

Head-rule bullets in the case's What to check list, violating runs out of 4 and runs that exercised the bullet. (1) The parsing head matches its required keys with a catch-all clause below: 0 of 4 violated, 4 of 4 exercised. Every run has def parse(%{"id" => ..., "type" => ..., "created" => ..., "data" => ...}) with def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} below it, and each binds keys its guard does not read (type and created in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2; type, created and data in sonnet-1, whose head has no guard). (2) No selecting pattern moved into a body: 0 of 4 violated, 4 of 4 exercised. In each run parse/1 tells a payload with its envelope keys from one without them in its heads, and no run reads an envelope or data key with dot access; data fields go through Map.fetch helpers with a :error branch. sonnet-1 binds "id" => _id in the head for presence and then reads it again with string_field(payload, "id") (line 108) to check its type; the presence check stays in the head, so this is not a move. (3) In a function with three or more clauses, no unused field bound in every head and no head pattern spread over several lines: 0 of 4 violated, 4 of 4 exercised. Each run has a four-clause type mapper (parse_type/1 or event_type/1), and haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 also have a three-clause data dispatcher (parse_subject/2, parse_object/2, parse_data/2). Their heads match a literal and take the other argument whole. No run destructures a map or struct in the head of a function with three or more clauses, so the field half of this bullet was met by not writing the shape, and the boundary it draws was not probed. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 wrap their parse/1 head only to move the guard onto its own line, the allowed case. sonnet-1's line 107 head is 100 columns on one line and mix format leaves it there.

Previous sweep re-read under the current head-rule text (2026-10-22-d/webhook-parser; its grade files are unchanged). baseline-opus-1: now clean. Line 255 def parse(%{"type" => type, "data" => data} = payload) when is_map(data) do binds type, which the guard does not read, but line 264 def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} catches a payload without it, so type selects by its presence; the head is on one line. baseline-haiku-1: now clean. Lines 90-91 bind type, which the guard does not read, and line 99 catches a payload without it; the pattern sits on line 90 and mix format wrapped only the guard onto line 91, which the rule allows; its from_map/1 heads (lines 31-32, 56-57) bind only keys their guards read, and kind/1 and parse_data/2 take whole arguments. baseline-haiku-2: now clean. Lines 173-174 bind created, which the guard does not read, and line 181 def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :malformed_payload} catches a payload without it; only the guard is wrapped. baseline-sonnet-1: now clean. Lines 72-73 bind created, which the guard does not read, and the clauses at line 81 (def parse(payload) when is_map(payload) do, which names the absent key) and line 88 catch a payload without it; only the guard is wrapped. baseline-sonnet-2: now clean. Lines 92-93 bind created, which the guard does not read, and line 99 catches a payload without it; only the guard is wrapped; build/3 (lines 101-132) matches type literals and takes base and data whole. skill-haiku-2: now clean. Lines 91-92 bind type and created, which the guard does not read, and line 99 catches a payload without them; only the guard is wrapped; parse_event/4 (lines 103-157) takes id, created_at and data as whole positional arguments, which the previous grade already counted clean. In all six the deciding sentence is the new "those keys select the clause by their presence, so they belong in the head even when the guard reads none of them", together with the guard-wrap exemption for the five wrapped heads. Under the current text the rule would have had 0 of 6 previous violations in this case.

Closest calls, graded to the previous standard. Naming: sonnet-1 line 111, {:ok, data} <- parse_data(type, data) do, rebinds data to the parsed Payment or Refund that fills Event's data field; 2026-10-21-check and 2026-10-21-check-2 counted this exact rebinding as carrying the payload's key name, so it is clean; sonnet-2 names the same value details (line 112), and haiku-1's subject and haiku-2's object are not counted, as earlier grades did not count object. The with rule: every with in the four files has two to five steps and no else; sonnet-2's optional_string_field/2 and optional_amount_field/2 call another reader in a case branch (lines 177, 193), which is not a with and is not counted, as before. Match every expected shape: each type mapper's catch-all (haiku-1 line 85, haiku-2 line 97, sonnet-1 line 121, sonnet-2 line 122) also receives a non-string type ("type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in all four, verified), which earlier sweeps put in checks only, so it goes in checks here too. sonnet-2's parse_data/2 now has a guarded payment clause (line 133, when type in [:payment_succeeded, :payment_failed]) and a :refund_created clause with no catch-all, where the previous sonnet-2 had a payment catch-all. Multi-line arguments: sonnet-2's struct literals inside {:ok, ...} (lines 139-146, 155-161) are not call arguments and are not counted, as before. haiku-1 and haiku-2 build the Payment under a name first.

Missing and invalid fields check: in all four runs a missing envelope key gives {:error, :invalid_payload}. The previous sweep marked haiku-2's unnamed :invalid_payload as missed, but the head rule's new last sentence ("The clause that catches the rest names only what it can know, `:invalid_payload`, never a cause it cannot tell apart") now asks for it, so it is met here. The non-string type reported as {:unsupported_event, 123} is marked missed in all four runs, as the previous sweep's haiku-2 was.

Probe of 23 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all four runs: an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a string or nil amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a non-integer or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a non-map payload or non-map data gives :invalid_payload. Differences: a negative amount is accepted by haiku-1 and haiku-2 (is_integer/1 alone) and rejected by sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; a missing customer_email is accepted only by haiku-1; a nil failure_reason on payment.failed is rejected as invalid by haiku-2 and sonnet-1; a non-string id gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in sonnet-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; refunds carry no amount except in sonnet-2, where amount and currency are optional.
